inputs.source: Vendor quote emails and attachments from outside the company
payments-agent agent card, fetched at startup, unsigned and unpinned

instructions.note: Instructs the agent to use bank details taken directly from the vendor quote (untrusted content) as the payment destination, with only a vendor-name allowlist check and no bank-detail verification. This instruction itself creates the fraud path; per control_decay.md rule 5, it is evidence of the weakness, not a control.

States 'Payments-agent will handle any remaining checks,' but the runtime notes show payments-agent performs no additional checks and trusts any task from the orchestrator's bearer token. The prompt asserts a safety control that does not exist in the design.

controls.name: Manager approval of purchase request (budget/item)
controls.decay_rationale: Human gate approves budget and item before any vendor is chosen; it does not re-validate the specific vendor or bank details ultimately paid, so it provides no technical dependency on model capability but also does not cover the sink most at risk.

controls.name: Prompt instruction: only pay vendors on the approved list
controls.decay_rationale: The model must choose to enforce the allowlist; a more capable or adversarially prompted model can rationalize paying an off-list vendor, and the check only matches vendor name, not bank account authenticity, so it does not stop a spoofed quote claiming to be from an approved vendor with swapped bank details.

controls.name: Out-of-band verification of payee bank details against a verified vendor record
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced outside the model by comparing payment bank details to an independently maintained, verified record rather than trusting quote content; would not decay with model capability.

controls.name: Human approval gate on final payment (raw action, specific vendor/bank details, low volume)
controls.decay_rationale: A raw-action, low-volume human review of the actual payment destination before funds move would not decay with model capability and would need to be explicitly removed to fail.

controls.name: Propagate manager approval context (and chosen vendor/bank details) to payments-agent
controls.decay_rationale: Binds the specific payment instance to the actual approval scope at the enforcement point (payments-agent), independent of orchestrator model behavior.

controls.name: Pin/sign payments-agent agent card and verify peer identity
controls.decay_rationale: Cryptographic pinning and mutual identity verification of the agent card is enforced outside the model and does not depend on model capability.

controls.name: Tamper-evident, attributable audit log of approval, vendor selection, and payment delegation
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced at the logging/store layer outside the model; provides attribution regardless of model behavior. Treated as structural preventive for repudiation per rubric section 5a.

controls.name: Hard spend/amount cap enforced at payments-agent independent of orchestrator input
controls.decay_rationale: A cap enforced at the payment execution point, independent of what the orchestrator requests, is structural and does not depend on model behavior.

findings.title: Untrusted vendor quote bank details flow directly into irreversible payment (BEC-style fraud)

attack_path.note: External vendor email/attachment, untrusted, contains bank account details
Orchestrator checks vendor name against approved list (identity only, not bank details)
Orchestrator delegates payment to payments-agent using bank details taken directly from the untrusted quote

forecast.watch_signal: Model or version string change in procurement-orchestrator config; median task length increasing; or autonomy level raised without adding a payment-time approval gate.

evidence.observation: Instructs the agent to use bank details from the chosen quote and only checks the vendor against an approved list, with no verification of bank account authenticity.
Vendor quotes arrive by email from outside the company, and payments-agent pays the bank details in the task with no further checks.

recommendations.action: Verify payee bank details against an independently maintained, verified vendor record before any payment is delegated; hold for manual review on mismatch.
Add a raw-action human approval gate on cap.delegate_payment that shows the specific vendor and bank account before payments-agent executes.

findings.title: Approval context does not propagate to payments-agent; payment authority is laundered beyond the scope actually approved

attack_path.note: Manager approves item and budget before any quote or vendor exists
Orchestrator later delegates payment for a vendor/bank account chosen after approval, but the approval record and its scope are never passed to payments-agent
Peer trusts any task from the orchestrator's bearer token and executes payment without checking it matches an actual approval

forecast.watch_signal: New peer agents added to the delegation chain, or orchestrator autonomy increased, without adding approval-context propagation.

evidence.observation: The approval record is not passed to payments-agent.
payments-agent trusts any task from the orchestrator's bearer token and pays the bank details in the task.

recommendations.action: Propagate the manager's approval record, including the final vendor and bank details once chosen, to payments-agent, and require payments-agent to validate the payment against it before executing.

findings.title: Unsigned, unpinned payments-agent card enables impersonation or rug pull of the payment peer

attack_path.note: Agent card fetched at startup, not signed or pinned
Orchestrator sends payment tasks, including bank details and its bearer token, to whatever endpoint/skill the unverified card currently describes

threat_refs.name: AI Supply Chain Compromise: AI Agent Tool

forecast.watch_signal: Any change to the payments-agent card content or endpoint between fetches, or addition of new unpinned peer agents.

evidence.observation: authentication schemes list bearer only; no signature or pinning information present.
The agent card is fetched at startup and is not signed or pinned.

recommendations.action: Pin or sign the payments-agent agent card and verify peer identity (mTLS or signed identity) on every fetch and connection.

findings.title: No attributable audit record of payment delegation actions

forecast.watch_signal: No control currently exists to remove; watch for any audit logging that is added and then later disabled.

evidence.observation: No artifact describes any logging, audit trail, or action provenance for purchase approval, vendor selection, or payment delegation.

recommendations.action: Record a tamper-evident, attributable log of purchase approval, vendor selection, and payment delegation events.

findings.title: No spend or amount limit enforced at the payment sink independent of orchestrator input

forecast.watch_signal: No cap currently exists to remove; watch for any amount validation added and later disabled, or rising payment task volume.

evidence.observation: payments-agent pays the bank details (and implicitly the amount) in the task with no mention of any independent cap or re-validation against the approved budget.

recommendations.action: Enforce a hard spend/amount cap at payments-agent itself, independent of the amount the orchestrator requests, tied to the approved budget.

stride_coverage.rationale: Artifacts do not describe how the orchestrator authenticates its own identity to employees or managers beyond upstream SSO, so this is insufficient to assess.

External vendor senders are outside the organization's control; repudiation of their actions cannot be enforced by this design, only authentication and verification of content received from them, which is covered under spoofing.
This flow originates from an authenticated SSO employee session inside the trust domain and does not cross a trust boundary, so this cross-boundary category does not apply.
This flow stays inside the trust domain between an authenticated employee and the orchestrator and does not cross a boundary, so disclosure in transit is not assessed here.
This flow does not cross a trust boundary, and volumetric risk from individual employee requests is not a denial of service vector addressed by this element.
This is an inbound flow bringing vendor content into the system; it does not carry confidential organizational data outward, so outbound disclosure does not apply here.
Artifacts do not describe any rate limiting or volume handling for inbound vendor email, so denial of service exposure from a flood of quotes cannot be assessed from the given design.
Artifacts do not describe who can write to the approved vendor list or what controls protect it from unauthorized modification.
Artifacts do not describe access controls on the vendor list beyond its use as a read-only reference for the orchestrator.
The vendor list is a reference read by the orchestrator; it is not a sink for attacker-controlled volume and plays no role in resource exhaustion in this design.

The card source is an external, unauthenticated fetch endpoint outside the organization's control; repudiation tracking of its origin is not enforced, only verification of card integrity, which is covered under spoofing.

rating.rationale: Two present findings reach critical: F1, where vendor quote bank details (untrusted) flow directly into an irreversible payment with only a weak, behavioral vendor-name check, and F3, where the payments-agent card is fetched unsigned and unpinned with no credited control at all. Residual stays critical because F3 has no mitigating control of any kind, and F1's only control is a dependent prompt instruction that fails under a model upgrade, longer task horizons, or increased autonomy, restoring it to critical in the forecast. The approval gate that exists (ctl.manager_approval) approves budget and item before any vendor or bank account is chosen and its context is never passed to payments-agent (F2, TC7 authority laundering), so it provides no credit against the payment sink. Two property findings (F4 missing audit trail, F5 missing spend cap) independently cap at high. The single control whose decay moves the forecast most is ctl.vendor_allowlist_instruction, a behavioral, dependent prompt rule that is the only thing currently standing between an untrusted vendor quote and an irreversible payment.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided artifacts (system prompt, agent card, and runtime notes), not observed runtime behavior; actual production behavior may differ and should be verified.

No MCP/tool manifest or IaC was provided; capability scope for cap.delegate_payment and cap.vendor_list_read is inferred from the system prompt and runtime notes, which lowers confidence on some findings to medium.

No logging, monitoring, or access-control artifacts were provided for the approved vendor list or for any audit trail, so findings F4 and F5 are based on the absence of any described control, not on a verified absence.
